topics.topic: How the enumeration for a member-valued field is identified
questions: For a row whose value kind is `member`, what determines the particular enumeration whose member value is accepted, and is that enumeration reference a fact of OwnerFormField?
When `value kind` is `member`, how is the particular closed enumeration whose member must be read identified?
For value kind `member`, what identifies the particular enumeration or vocabulary whose member the text denotes?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 about identifying the enumeration for a member-valued row, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: How an enumeration-reading row identifies its applicable enumeration or allowed values
quotes:
A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0. A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
member's value.
precedent.why: The later contract makes the row identify an exact typed destination through its carrier and path, so that destination field supplies the enumeration rather than a separate allowed-value fact in OwnerFormField.

precedent.topic: Which owner-interface pages, actions, forms, and queries the catalog and its rules cover
quotes:
Which action a request names, by its
method and path, and whether it is a change or touches an uploaded file, are
the rows of the data provider's `OWNER_ACTIONS`; its target is the query
parameter `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` names, its CSRF value the form field
`OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` names, every other field it reads or a page writes a row
of `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (owner, 2026-11-25), the session cookie's name
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and its attributes
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, and a page's HTTP status the service API's
`SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS` and `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` (owner, 2026-11-24).

Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`). A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0.
precedent.why: The later texts make OWNER_FORM_FIELDS global to every non-target, non-CSRF owner-interface field that a page writes or a request reads, with rows selected by carrier and destination path rather than by a page or action fact.

`POST` request's the fields of its `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
body, or of the upload's multipart head. Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`). A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0.
judgement.why: The later contract makes form versus query depend on the request method, while carrier independently selects whether the row's destination path is in OwnerRequest or OwnerValues; no third query carrier is used.

The action is the row of the imported `OWNER_ACTIONS` constant whose method

quotes:
A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written

quotes:
A row of the owner form table: one field an owner page writes into a form
or a query, and the owner interface reads back (owner, 2026-11-25). The row
gives the field's name, its path in the owner request or its values, with a
tuple's position marked; which of the two it fills; and how its text is
read: as text, as an integer, as true or false, or as an enumeration
member's value. A field no row names is not read. The table holds the names
so that the page and the reader cannot name a field differently (Route B
runs of 2026-11-25).

Facts: the field's name, which holds its path and the mark of each tuple
position in it, so that two rows of different paths are different rows; what
it fills; how its text is read.

Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`). A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0. A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
member's value. A union's fields are the rows of all its variants, and its
discriminator chooses the variant. A field the form leaves out is none,
and a tuple none of whose positions are given is empty. A field whose name
no row names is not read and changes nothing. A form that repeats a name,
gives a text the row's `reads_as` cannot read or leaves a gap in a tuple's
positions cannot be read.
judgement.divergence: If two rows have the same submitted name but different carrier or reading facts, one implementation rejects the release catalogue as ambiguous, while another accepts it and applies the submitted text to both destinations; the owner and the receiving product action observe refusal versus a constructed request.
judgement.why: The texts make OWNER_FORM_FIELDS a global name-based catalogue and forbid repeated names in a submitted form, but never state whether two distinct catalogue rows may themselves share a name or how such a match is resolved.

quotes: Not persisted; a constant of the release.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
